walkthroughs.body_html:
Oscillations — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Oscillations brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Oscillations.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: Damping is critical.
The driving frequency matches the natural frequency.
Amplitude is zero.
Energy is conserved.

mcqs.q: Heavy damping in a car suspension causes:
options: Continuous oscillation at high amplitude.
Slow return to equilibrium without oscillation.
Resonance.
Increased natural frequency.

mcqs.q: Why is the electric field between parallel charged plates considered uniform?
options: Field strength is constant in magnitude and direction throughout the region (away from edges), unlike the inverse-square field of a point charge.
The field still decreases with the inverse square of distance — uniform just means it's smooth.
Because the plates are uniform in shape.
Because gravity in the glass pulls the light down.

mcqs.q: In the ideal gas equation pV = nRT, what must the temperature T be measured in?
options: Because gravity in the glass pulls the light down.
Either Celsius or Kelvin gives the same result.
Kelvin — the absolute temperature scale.
Whatever units make the numbers work out neatly.

mcqs.q: Why does light bend when it enters a denser medium like glass?
options: Because it slows down — the change in speed at the boundary causes the wavefront to bend (towards the normal).
Because gravity in the glass pulls the light down.
Because the medium is denser, it physically blocks part of the light and forces it to turn.
Whatever units make the numbers work out neatly.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Natural frequency”?
options: The frequency at which a system oscillates when displaced and released without external driving.
Reduction of amplitude of oscillations due to dissipation of energy as heat.
Oscillation produced by a periodic external driving force.
The minimum damping that returns the system to equilibrium without oscillation in the shortest time.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Forced oscillation”?
options: Reduction of amplitude of oscillations due to dissipation of energy as heat.
Oscillation produced by a periodic external driving force.
The minimum damping that returns the system to equilibrium without oscillation in the shortest time.
The frequency at which a system oscillates when displaced and released without external driving.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Resonance”?
options: Large-amplitude oscillation when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency.
Oscillation produced by a periodic external driving force.
The minimum damping that returns the system to equilibrium without oscillation in the shortest time.
The frequency at which a system oscillates when displaced and released without external driving.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Critical damping”?
options: The minimum damping that returns the system to equilibrium without oscillation in the shortest time.
Reduction of amplitude of oscillations due to dissipation of energy as heat.
Oscillation produced by a periodic external driving force.
The frequency at which a system oscillates when displaced and released without external driving.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Free oscillation”?
options: Oscillation of a system at its natural frequency with no external driving force.
Large-amplitude oscillation when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency.
Reduction of amplitude of oscillations due to dissipation of energy as heat.
The minimum damping that returns the system to equilibrium without oscillation in the shortest time.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Damping”?
options: Large-amplitude oscillation when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency.
The minimum damping that returns the system to equilibrium without oscillation in the shortest time.
Reduction of amplitude of oscillations due to dissipation of energy as heat.
Oscillation produced by a periodic external driving force.
